summary: Delphine Menant (1850–1932) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under James Darmesteter. In 1900, she served as chargée de mission dans l'Inde for the Guimet Museum.
Demchok Dorje studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Denis Sinor (1916–2011) worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Paul Pelliot and at the University of Cambridge, later holding posts at Cambridge (1948–1962) and Indiana University Bloomington (1962–1986).

Denis Twitchett (1925–2006) was a sinologist and historian educated at SOAS and St Catharine's College, Cambridge. He held positions at the University of London, the University of Cambridge, and Princeton University (1980–1994).

Denise Bernot (1922–2016) was a linguist who studied at the École des chartes and École nationale des langues orientales vivantes. She held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from approximately 1960 to 1989.

Denma Lochö Rinpoche (1928–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric College. He served at the University of Calcutta, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and Namgyal Monastery.

Dennis A. Johnson specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Magister der Philosophie under Klaus-Dieter Mathes at the University of Vienna, where he was attested at the South Asian, Tibetan and Buddhist Studies Library in 2022.
Dennis Genpo Merzel (born 1944) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Southern California, the USC Rossier School of Education, and under Taizan Maezumi.

Dennis Hirota (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at UC Berkeley and Nagoya University, he held posts at Chikushi Jogakuen University, Harvard University, Hongwanji International Center, and Ryukoku University.

Denys de Saumarez Bray (1875–1951) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Balliol College, Oxford, from around 1894 to 1898. He served as a member of the Council of India between 1930 and 1937.

Denzaburo Yoshizawa (1924–2003) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji from around 1947 to 1950. He held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (1960–1987) and Iryo Sosei University (1989–1999).
Denzil Ibbetson (1847–1908) worked in Indology and other fields. He completed his education at St Peter's College, Adelaide, and studied mathematics at St John's College between around 1865 and 1869.
Deocar Schmid (1791–1828) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at the University of Jena from 1808 to 1813 and studied under Carl Christian Erhard Schmid.

Derek F. Maher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his degrees from Evergreen State College and the University of Virginia, where he studied under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held posts at Virginia, UNC Greensboro, and East Carolina University.

Dermot Killingley (born 1935) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Oxford, Merton College, and SOAS under David Friedman and Arnold Kunst. He held posts at the University of Malaya, Newcastle University, and Vienna.
Dermott Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Trinity College Dublin, Leiden University, and UCLA, completing his PhD under William M. Bodiford.

Dessislava Vendova is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies educated at Sofia, BLCU, Peking, Kyoto, and Columbia. She has held posts at NYU, the Graduate Theological Union, MFA Boston, Holy Cross, and UMass Boston.

Detlef Ingo Lauf (1936–2001) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held professorships at the C. G. Jung Institute Zürich, California Institute of Integral Studies, Ohio University, and Columbia Pacific University.
Devachandra Bharati 'Prakhar' is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who became a Ph.D. research scholar at Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Rohilkhand University beginning in 2021.

Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (1875–1950) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910) and Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of India's Western Circle (1911–1917).
